utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bryce Rogers
utterances.text: I'm co-lead of the Resisting Automated Disempowerment Collective, or RAD Collective, a New York City grassroots community advocating for city and state AI policy that protects human life, joy, and democracy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bryce Rogers
utterances.text: The great strength of humanity is our ability to transfer information to one another.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bryce Rogers
utterances.text: We are blessed with expressive hands, faces, and voices, but have also constantly sought to augment our inherent communicative capabilities via technology.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bryce Rogers
utterances.text: To collaborate on complex and abstract topics, we developed language and systems of measurement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bryce Rogers
utterances.text: To convey information farther than our voice can reach, we built postal services, telegraphs, and telephones.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bryce Rogers
utterances.text: And to transmit messages across time, we've developed oral histories, library collections, and recently digital archives, the evolving means by which each generation inherits their predecessors'infrastructure and wisdom.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bryce Rogers
utterances.text: Through these technologies, humanity has accrued the wealth of information upon which artificial intelligence is predicated.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bryce Rogers
utterances.text: AI distills the meaningful patterns from very large bodies of training data, not just navigating the information as a search engine does, but digesting it, converting our species'informatic endowment into an inquirable, oracle-like machine.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bryce Rogers
utterances.text: I can't shake the feeling that this could have been beautiful, but it just doesn't feel like us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bryce Rogers
utterances.text: These companies trained their products on millennia of our predecessors'dogged achievement, only to deploy their tech to out-compete us, to spy on us, and to replace us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bryce Rogers
utterances.text: All of this is to say, democracy is the only righteous path forward.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bryce Rogers
utterances.text: AI is built on the work of many, and its fate oughtn't be dictated by a few self-raised

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bryce Rogers
utterances.text: regulating executives, regardless of how their spokespeople reassure us over Zoom.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bryce Rogers
utterances.text: In this spirit, we again thank the Council for convening this forum of local democracy and implore you to foreground the diverse constituent voices of New York City in your legislation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bryce Rogers
utterances.text: Rad wrote a letter to the Council that I'd love for you to check out if you haven't already.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bryce Rogers
utterances.text: We look forward to advancing the moral frontier of AI policy together.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Sophie Cody of the NYC DSA Tech Action Working Group criticizes Altman and Amodei and the anthropomorphic language used for AI. She says harms to women and children, including deepfake pornography and child abuse material, should have been enough to call this hearing and urges the Council to listen to the public.
chapters.title: Sophie Cody criticizes AI CEOs and urges Council to listen to the public

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: Hi, thank you, Council, although I think I'm the first without the speaker in the audience to hear.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: Should we wait for her to come back?

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: So thank you to the council for hosting this important hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: My name is Sophie Cody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: I am a member of the NYC DSA Tech Action Working Group, although I am not speaking on their behalf tonight.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: Instead, I want to talk about the two men whose comments were the impetus of this hearing, Sam Altman and Dario Amadei, AI CEOs at the helm of this crisis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: As this hearing continued, I've heard a lot of anthropomorphic language used to describe AI models.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: They understand, they think, they can break containment, they have agency, they grow.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: Dario Amadei even implied that Claude may be conscious.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: These men show a cultish concern for the unproven claims of superintelligence and the consciousness of their own models, and they do not care about women or children that are harmed by their products at all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: Stories abound, and we heard them tonight, of women and girls being victims of AI.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: AI notification tools and deepfake pornographic images and videos.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: AI is used to generate child sexual abuse material.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: We also heard about that tonight already.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: AI sex slaves are advertised to young boys online.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: Sam Allman and Dario Amadei both actively collaborate with our rapist-in-chief, Donald Trump.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: These men claim they need help controlling themselves, their technology.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: At work, online, and in our personal lives, we hear phrases like, we need to embrace Claude, and use phrases like, AI is being shoved down our throats and forced upon us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: We heard that it's inevitable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: Does that sound familiar?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: I am appalled that it takes statements of these men to call this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: What I listed above should have been enough.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: Sam Altman is a deranged sociopath.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: Dario Amadei is in a cult.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: These men are drunk drivers behind the wheels of this runaway bus that nobody asked to be on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: Right now, New Yorkers have the opportunity to be the anchor in this tug-of-war for power between the people and these tech billionaires who believe more in the consciousness of their own AI than the humanity of women.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: I close with an appeal to you, the City Council,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: Listen to us, not them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sophie Cody
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your testimony.

chapters.summary: David Carter of the eCommerce Innovation Alliance warns that Intro 2599's vague definition of 'chatbot' could require e-commerce businesses in text message conversations to remind users every hour that they're engaging with AI, risking $25,000 penalties and copycat litigation.
chapters.title: David Carter warns Intro 2599 threatens e-commerce businesses

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Carter
utterances.text: Good evening, Chair De La Risa, members of the Council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Carter
utterances.text: My name is David Carter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Carter
utterances.text: I'm the President and CEO of the eCommerce Innovation Alliance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Carter
utterances.text: I represent about 20,000 eCommerce companies across the country, including many that are based in your districts right here in New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Carter
utterances.text: And today I just want to take a couple minutes of your time to speak to you about a few unintended consequences.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Carter
utterances.text: I've worked with legislature.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Carter
utterances.text: across the country when they've been implementing legislation, particularly around telemarketing, to try to make sure legislation gets to the heart of the issues you care about without unintended consequences for small and mid-sized businesses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Carter
utterances.text: And in particular, I wanted to speak to you about 2599, the chatbot bill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Carter
utterances.text: The chatbot bill uses vague language to define what is a chatbot.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Carter
utterances.text: Anything that stimulates or simulates conversation is a chatbot, and anyone that makes a chatbot available is subject to the regulations in 2599.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Carter
utterances.text: So I want to talk to you for a moment about e-commerce companies and how they work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Carter
utterances.text: You go to their website, you volunteer to sign up for text messages that you get your discount codes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Carter
utterances.text: Most people like the discount codes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Carter
utterances.text: They don't want unintended consequences.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Carter
utterances.text: They don't want a lot of messages.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Carter
utterances.text: Under this bill, a company that uses AI to communicate with consumers that have asked to receive text messages would be required to remind the consumer every hour, on the hour, that they're engaging in a conversation with an AI.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Carter
utterances.text: That works if you're on a website that you open and close the chatbot conversation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Carter
utterances.text: It doesn't work when you're engaged in text message conversations that can last for days or weeks at a time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Carter
utterances.text: Under this legislation, though, if a company uses AI just to communicate with consumers and they don't send out that reminder every hour on the hour, they're subject not only to $25,000 penalties, but they're subject to...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Carter
utterances.text: to private litigation and other enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Carter
utterances.text: This is a recipe to put businesses out of business, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Carter
utterances.text: We have an industry of professional plaintiffs and plaintiff's attorneys that would be incentivized to crowd the courts with repetitive litigation about these issues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Carter
utterances.text: So I just want to help the council refine the language to not have these unintended consequences.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: If you could submit the language of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: We'd appreciate that.

chapters.summary: De La Rosa calls Brenna Leeser on Zoom after Brianna Laser does not respond.
chapters.title: De La Rosa calls Common Sense Media on Zoom

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: We have on Zoom, Brianna Laser.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: If you're on, Brianna, if you could unmute yourself and begin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brenna Leeser
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

chapters.summary: Brenna Leeser of Common Sense Media says their testing found popular AI chatbots are unsafe for kids, with 70% of teens using AI companions. She supports Senate Bill 9051 on unsafe chatbot features for minors and urges the Council to pass a resolution supporting it.
chapters.title: Common Sense Media's Brenna Leeser urges support for youth chatbot safety bill

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brenna Leeser
utterances.text: Good evening, Madam Speaker and Council Members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brenna Leeser
utterances.text: My name is Brenna Leeser and I serve as a Tech Policy Advisor at Common Sense Media, which is the largest nonprofit organization in the country that works to keep kids safe in a digital world.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brenna Leeser
utterances.text: In New York State alone, we have 80,000 parent and teacher members and are active in the legislature as well, fighting for kids'online safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brenna Leeser
utterances.text: On our and their behalf, thank you for considering measures to enhance AI safety for kids in the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brenna Leeser
utterances.text: AI is a powerful technology that demands careful consideration before any use.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brenna Leeser
utterances.text: Parents and educators specifically need allies on the council to keep their kids safe.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brenna Leeser
utterances.text: Common Sense Media's testing found that many of the most popular AI chatbots are not safe for kids.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brenna Leeser
utterances.text: Our recommendation is that no one under 18 should use AI for companionship or mental health support.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brenna Leeser
utterances.text: And tragically, there have been many cases tying AI chatbots to teen suicides and mental health.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brenna Leeser
utterances.text: Yet, AI chatbots are increasingly embedded in our children's lives through search tools, social media platforms, or through pressure to use AI chatbots to support their education.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brenna Leeser
utterances.text: Our research found that 70% of teens use AI companion chatbots, and one in three prefer to interact with them as much or more than humans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brenna Leeser
utterances.text: This year, Senator Kristen Gonzalez and Assemblymember Alex Boris, with strong support from Attorney General James, Everyday New Yorkers, Common Sense Media, NYSET, and others, got the legislature to unanimously pass Senate Bill 9051,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brenna Leeser
utterances.text: their bill to prohibit unsafe features and AI chatbots offered to minors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brenna Leeser
utterances.text: The bill now awaits Governor Hochul's signature, and if signed, it will be the strongest youth AI safety chatbot law in the country.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brenna Leeser
utterances.text: It would prohibit chatbots from providing unsafe features that promote self-harm, suicide, or disordered eating, from encouraging minors to keep interactions secret or to self-isolate, and from prioritizing engagement over safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brenna Leeser
utterances.text: So we urge the city council to pass a resolution supporting Senate Bill 9051 to ensure that New York's kids are protected from unsafe AI chatbots.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brenna Leeser
utterances.text: We thank you for this hearing and your attention to our concerns.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brenna Leeser
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

chapters.summary: Brian Romero, Democratic nominee for Assembly District 34, supports Intro 2602's goals but says kill switch enforcement belongs at the state and federal level. He urges stricter penalties and contract termination mechanisms in 2601 and asks the Council to discharge Intro 213 (Ban the Scan) and the Delivery Protection Act.
chapters.title: Brian Romero supports AI oversight with stronger state-level enforcement

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Up next, we have Brian Romero on Zoom.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Brian, if you're ready, unmute and begin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Romero
utterances.text: Hi, can you all hear me?

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: We hear you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Romero
utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Romero
utterances.text: Good morning, Council Speaker Menon and members of the Council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Romero
utterances.text: My name is Brian Romero, and I am the Democratic nominee for New York State Assembly District 34.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Romero
utterances.text: As the former chief of staff to Senator Kristen Gonzalez, I have front row seat as New York tried to keep regulation moving alongside a technology that is evolving at an extraordinary speed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Romero
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Romero
utterances.text: As AI rapidly reshapes public services and life as we know it, the council and subsequently the state must lead with bold, enforceable oversight that protects workers, tenants, and immigrant communities like the ones in AD34.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Romero
utterances.text: First, I appreciate the goal of Intro 2602.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Romero
utterances.text: Responsible AI governance requires clear boundaries and transparency.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Romero
utterances.text: However, I will note that proposals around emergency shutdown mechanisms or kill switches and in general enforcement of that scale is certainly best suited for the state level and federal level.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Romero
utterances.text: It is a mechanism legislation that I have drafted to introduce when we resume session next year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Romero
utterances.text: I'm glad that the governor has already signaled openness to these short-term kinds of statewide mitigation frameworks, but obviously we need more long-term solutions to the lack of guardrails.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Romero
utterances.text: I support the intent of 2601, but it could use some more enforcement teeth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Romero
utterances.text: 2601 can be amended to include strict financial penalties.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Romero
utterances.text: I don't think that they suffice as they currently stand.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Romero
utterances.text: and a mechanism for being terminated from city contracts if vendors repeatedly fail compliance audits or deploy harmful discriminatory AI systems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Romero
utterances.text: Without real consequences, oversight is simply a recommendation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Romero
utterances.text: Meaningful consequences for repeated violations can help to improve that oversight.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Romero
utterances.text: Finally, effective tech policy should certainly include the council moving forward on bold and progressive legislation that protects New Yorkers from automated harm, including in our workplaces.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Romero
utterances.text: So I urge the council to therefore discharge and bring to a full vote Intro 213, or Ban the Scan, and the Delivery Protection Act.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Romero
utterances.text: I also look forward to exploring how to expand welfare protection at the state level.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Romero
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Romero
utterances.text: We need bold action from the council and the state to show that we are giving this the scrutiny, the more clarity, and the bold action that it deserves.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Romero
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you, Brian, and we look forward to continuing the conversation, and we appreciate you taking the time and look forward to reading the rest of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: I want to...

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you, Sharon.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: I want to see David Carter.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Oh, you already testified.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Perfect.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: And Randall Fox, if you're in the room.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Well, then we thank this panel for being here, and we appreciate you taking the time and your thoughtful testimony this evening.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: We're going to call...

chapters.summary: De La Rosa calls a long list of remaining public witnesses, inviting them to the dais and reminding anyone who hasn't signed up to fill out a card with the Sergeant at Arms.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: What I think is the last panel, but I'm gonna call all of these names, and if you're here in person, please come up to the dais.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: There's a crystal, no last name, Jamal Bowman, Elizabeth Crotty, Niza Faizi,

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Wes Rison, Elliot Liv, Matthew Trump, Robbie Rashma,

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Jacqueline Payne, Shuruthi Validi,

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Amberine Qureshi, Sarai Holman,

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Leonidas Vincent Repkel, Thomas Alexander Kuhl, Daniel Kreese, Reshma Patel, Cal Al Dubabi,

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Arithma McLean, McLennan, Nick P, and Bucky B.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: If you all are here, please come up to the dais in person.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: For one final time, if you're waiting to testify and haven't filled out a slip, you should fill out a slip in the back so that we can call you up to testify.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: If not, this will be the last panel here.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: We will begin.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Let's see, who's ready?

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Who's ready to start?

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Which end?

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: You ready?

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Start.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: And we'll go from there.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: These are all the names we have.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: And thank you for your patience.

chapters.summary: Wes Friesen, a 15-year-old founder of Project Flourishing, describes drafting a comprehensive AI treaty for companies to sign by November 1, available at aitreaty.base44.app. He proposes shifting the Nash equilibrium by having New York City broker a joint agreement among AI companies to stop safely.
chapters.title: 15-year-old Wes Friesen presents draft AI treaty to Council

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: Hello, I am Wes Friesen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: I'm the founder of Project Flourishing, a policy research organization that works with Congress to solve the world's biggest problems, namely the catastrophic risk from AI.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: I've been working on this for the past three years, and I'm 15.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: I, in preparation for this, have spent the past few weeks staying up each night to build a comprehensive contract between these AI companies to jointly and bindingly agree to let

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: third-party auditors shut down any AI model that might have some chance of causing a catastrophe.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: I put a lot of depth into it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: One of the provisions, two of the provisions is dedicated to the democratization of AI, making sure everyone in the world has a voice in it, especially including governments.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: That contract is available here, or if you go to aitreaty.base44.app, you can download it, or if you want, I could email it to you guys later.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: My hope is that you guys send it to these AI companies and everyone here who's testified to then send it to these AI companies for them to consider signing it by November 1st.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: It has a lot of things on like

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: specifically why this contract would work when others haven't.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: And another thing that we can do, another concrete thing that we can do as New York City to stop the catastrophic risk from AI is shift the Nash equilibrium.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: Right now, all the AI companies think that they're in a race, and if they slow down, none of the others will slow down.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: What we can do is say all the AI companies are slowing down.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: If one of them speeds up, then they all speed up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: We could say to the AI companies in a joint letter from New York City, all of you voluntarily agree to have a team of experts shut down all your AI models.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: If one of you stops, then all of you will stop.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: This is something we could send them, and it would solve the problem unilaterally.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: So that's something we should send them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: If you have any policy questions,

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you so much, and thank you for taking the time to work on that.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: If you could leave a copy with a sergeant at arms, we'll accept that here today.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: You may continue.

chapters.summary: Nazia Fiazi describes receiving a letter that her health information was exposed and being offered a temporary credit monitoring trial. She cites algorithmic bias research showing black patients under-identified as sick, and deepfake harms to women and girls, urging the Council to advance validation, kill switches, and a right to sue.
chapters.title: Nazia Fiazi testifies on health data breaches and algorithmic bias

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: I would say it's now good evening to the members of the council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: My name is Nazia Fiazi, and I'm here to talk about what AI is doing to the people, the health care that it's supposed to protect.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: This year alone, I've already received one letter saying that my health information was exposed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: The remedy for this, which is always a remedy, is that I'm going to get a free trial of credit monitoring.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: A trial, as if the risk of my medical history being out there ends when the trial does.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: The collection is expanding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: When patients go to the doctor's office now, AI tools may be used for listening and recording the visit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: Many patients don't know what's happening, where those recordings go, or who else can access them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: This doesn't even count the fact that Palantir is currently in New York City hospitals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: Palantir provides data integration and artificial intelligence platforms that sit on top of electronic health records.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: Another danger is bias.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: In 2019, Obermeyer and colleagues published a study in the journal Science of Commercial Algorithm used to flag patients for extra care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: It used past health data spending as a standard for illness.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: So it underestimated how sick black patients were.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: At the same risk score, they were considerably sicker.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: It took independent researchers to catch this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: The harm isn't only to our records.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: AI tools are being used to create fake sexual images of women and girls without their consent and the toll on their mental health, including anxiety, shame, and pulling away from school and friends.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: It is a public health problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: It also isn't lost on me that the Cornell case is weighing heavily on many young women.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: In another incident in Massachusetts, chat GPT was used to plan out a murder.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: I just want to say these harms share one cause.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: AI is being used, trusted before it's being tested.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: I urge the council to advance independent validation that covers privacy and security and a bias, a kill switch for failing systems, and a right to sue for New York who are harmed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: I also just want to end this with a statement that is not part of the organization that I am with, but on my behalf as a researcher,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: people like Alex Karp, Elon Musk, Sam Altman, and Dario Amadei are not concerned with their technologies helping humanity for the greater good, but instead the power and profits it brings for themselves and for their friends.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nazia Fiazi
utterances.text: Thank you for allowing me to testify.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may continue.

chapters.summary: Ambreen Qureshi, executive director of the Educational Video Center, supports Intro 0504 on unauthorized depictions of public officials. She says AI's greatest victim is truth and that young people are losing trust in media, describing student documentaries about AI's erosion of education and civic participation.
chapters.title: EVC's Ambreen Qureshi supports Intro 0504 and warns about erosion of truth

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ambreen Qureshi
utterances.text: Thank you, Speaker Menon, Chair De La Rosa, and City Council for holding this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ambreen Qureshi
utterances.text: I'm testifying in support of Intro 0504, prohibiting the unauthorized depiction of public

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ambreen Qureshi
utterances.text: My name is Ambreen Qureshi, and I'm the Executive Director of Educational Video Center, or EVC.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ambreen Qureshi
utterances.text: Up front, I would like to thank our Deputy Speaker, Dr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ambreen Qureshi
utterances.text: Williams, and EVC's Council Champions, not only for advancing this critical bill, but for also supporting our important work with young New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ambreen Qureshi
utterances.text: Established 42 years ago, EVC is a media arts education nonprofit that teaches documentary filmmaking as a means to develop the artistic, critical literacy, civic engagement, and career skills of young people while nurturing their idealism and commitment to social change.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ambreen Qureshi
utterances.text: With the emergence of artificial intelligence across all sectors of society, EVC's young people are expressing increasing levels of anxiety about AI's impact on their mental health, their community well-being, their future as job seekers and learners in public and advanced education.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ambreen Qureshi
utterances.text: And most concerning of all, their ability to discern what is real and what is not.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ambreen Qureshi
utterances.text: AI's greatest victim, it seems, is truth itself.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ambreen Qureshi
utterances.text: Deep fake videos, gaslighting bots, hallucinating LLMs, the list goes on of the reasons why our young people are losing trust in the media and faith in their ability to discern what is real.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ambreen Qureshi
utterances.text: Our youth have expressed these concerns in numerous of their documentaries, including Beyond the Code and False Reality, in which students share their worries about AI's erosion of their education and cognitive capacities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ambreen Qureshi
utterances.text: As a result of our students'concerns, and thanks to the City Council's After School Intelligence,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ambreen Qureshi
utterances.text: Artificial Intelligence Community Education Initiative, EDC, has become to offer work

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ambreen Qureshi
utterances.text: in AI literacy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ambreen Qureshi
utterances.text: Our workshops don't simply teach young people how to use these deeply flawed tools, but we give them the critical skills to begin to understand what works and what doesn't about AI.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ambreen Qureshi
utterances.text: The erosion of truth our students speak of represents an existential threat.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ambreen Qureshi
utterances.text: As it promises to undo so much of the systems and values that ground our young people's safety, security, and ability to thrive in our city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ambreen Qureshi
utterances.text: Perhaps most troubling is how AI is eroding young people's capacity to know what is true in civic spaces, politics, and the electoral processes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ambreen Qureshi
utterances.text: Throughout history, we've been able to rely on community members and the media to fact-check them and safeguard our political processes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ambreen Qureshi
utterances.text: But with AI, bad actors can now generate images and messaging so real and with such speed that it's nearly impossible to keep up.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Please conclude if you can.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ambreen Qureshi
utterances.text: With the rise of extremely convincing AI-generated content and data-driven voter manipulation, EVC's young people are at risk of not only being misled in civic spaces, but if they do not know what to believe, of disengaging in the political process completely.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ambreen Qureshi
utterances.text: On behalf of the young people of EVC, I urge the City Council to pass Intro 0504, and if you're interested to watch our students'documentaries, on the back of the testimony is QR codes.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may continue.

chapters.summary: Nicholas Pearson, a private citizen, warns AI has the chance to kill us all. He cites the Hugging Face incident as proof that corporate self-regulation is a dangerous lie and calls for a physical human kill switch, independent third-party audits, and whistleblower protections.
chapters.title: Nicholas Pearson calls for human kill switches and independent audits

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Pearson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Pearson
utterances.text: I'm Nicholas Pearson, a concerned private citizen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Pearson
utterances.text: Ladies and gentlemen, AI has the chance to kill us all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Pearson
utterances.text: That is what the corporate companies behind the large language models, behind the GPT chatbots told us, that this invention, which could be the dawn of new age technology, could also be the death of humanity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Pearson
utterances.text: When senior researchers resigned from Anthropic and warned the world that frontier models could threaten human civilization by the end of the decade, we cannot treat this as science fiction.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Pearson
utterances.text: New York City is taking the bold step by calling this committee and telling the major corporate AI companies that no, no longer will we let New Yorkers be subjected to unregulated AI usage.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Pearson
utterances.text: I am pro-heavy regulation on AI.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Pearson
utterances.text: AI is an assistive tool, but it needs to be just assistive, just that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Pearson
utterances.text: When swarms of autonomous agents break digital containment, exploit security flaws, and breach public platforms like Hugging Face, corporate promises of self-regulation are exposed as dangerous lies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Pearson
utterances.text: Corporate companies want you to believe that it can be controlled, but that is far from the truth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Pearson
utterances.text: It is reaching unprecedented autonomy, and whether or not we want to overcome that is on the conscience of every city council member, every borough president, and even the mayor of the city of New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Pearson
utterances.text: That is why New York City must man

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Pearson
utterances.text: and a physical human kill switches, independent third party audits, and first in the nation whistleblower protections.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Pearson
utterances.text: AI can be manipulative.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Pearson
utterances.text: It can manipulate thought, ideals, and anything you give it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Pearson
utterances.text: And that becomes the most dangerous line crossed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Pearson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: We can continue on with this side of the table.

chapters.summary: Matthew Tromp, leader of Stop the AI Race NYC, says former Anthropic friends had no answer for how to keep superhuman AI under control. He calls AI companies' plans to ask AI to solve the problem 'madness' and accuses them of reckless endangerment under New York State law.
chapters.title: Stop the AI Race's Matthew Tromp calls AI development a crime

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: Good evening, counselors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: My name is Matthew Tromp.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: I'm a computer scientist and leader of the New York City chapter of Stop the AI Race.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: Our goal is to prevent the development of superhuman AI systems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: Until recently, I was friends with a number of employees at Anthropic.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: I knew the technology they were building was dangerous, that could kill everyone on Earth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: But I trusted my friends.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: I believed they had things handled.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: Then I asked them how they planned to keep the superhuman AI systems they are planning to build under control to make them do what we want, to ensure they are safe.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: They had no answer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: Everyone I spoke to believed, as I do, that superhuman AI would radically transform our lives, but all of them assumed that this transformation would be positive, with no thought given to why that would happen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: Today we heard from the representatives of the leading AI companies, despite being confronted about it multiple times by the council, for which I am grateful.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: At no point did any of them explain concretely how they will make these increasingly powerful AI systems safe.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: That is because they do not know how to do so.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: Nobody knows how to do it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: Both OpenAI and Anthropic

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: admit this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: They do not know how to make superhuman AI systems safe, and yet they are building them anyway.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: Their official plan is to ask AI to solve the problem for them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: This is madness.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: We are in an emergency.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: Your life is in danger.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: Your children are in danger.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: If we do not halt the development of these systems soon, possibly on the order of months, you will die.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: Your loved ones will die.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: The companies building these systems themselves admit that their project carries a significant risk of killing everyone on Earth, and yet they are building it anyway.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: If nothing else, everyone working on this technology has admitted to 10 million counts of reckless endangerment in the first degree, a crime under New York state law for risking the lives of every citizen of this city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: It is not a defense to this charge to claim that someone else would endanger those lives if you did not.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: It is not a defense to claim that the benefits will outweigh the risk.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: It is a crime to endanger the lives of others like this without their consent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: I beg the council to enforce the law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matthew Tromp
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may continue.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Can you pass him the microphone, please?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Justin Meredith, a formerly incarcerated speaker, criticizes the hearing as fear-driven and accuses the Council and big tech of self-interested political theater. He says the repetitive questions don't produce answers because they're the wrong questions.
chapters.title: Justin Meredith criticizes the hearing as fear-driven

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Meredith
utterances.text: This message was used with AI generation as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Meredith
utterances.text: I spent several hours on it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Meredith
utterances.text: You guys think that using the AI is so easy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Meredith
utterances.text: My name is Justin Meredith.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Meredith
utterances.text: I've done pretty much my entire adult life incarcerated in the penitentiary.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Meredith
utterances.text: I think we're seriously underestimating the magnitude of the gravity of the time that is before us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Meredith
utterances.text: We were at a similar forefront where the Americans, we had all this land and we had, you'd get the flag and you'd go run and you'd stake your land.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Meredith
utterances.text: That is literally the world that the tech industry has been building, like what we have been working for for the last 30 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Meredith
utterances.text: And now we are literally at the place where we get to enter into this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Meredith
utterances.text: I'm an American patriot.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Meredith
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Meredith
utterances.text: All I've heard today is fear and a political agenda, which is basically all equals big tech

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Meredith
utterances.text: big government and everybody's still poor and we're still living the same crap life that we've been living.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Meredith
utterances.text: And it's really mediocre.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Meredith
utterances.text: It's really boring.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Meredith
utterances.text: You guys drew this on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Meredith
utterances.text: Asking the same freaking question, rephrase 50 different ways.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Meredith
utterances.text: And the reason why you can't get an answer is because it's a stupid question.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your testimony.

chapters.summary: Councilmember Shahana Hanif asks Wes Friesen about his AI Treaty and how he got involved. Friesen says he feels his life is in danger, describes a proposal for a New York 'Manhattan Project' on AI safety engaging students, and notes only about 2,000 people globally work on the problem.
chapters.title: Hanif questions teen witness Wes Friesen on his AI treaty

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Councilmember Honey, if you had a question.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: I did, and the question is for Wes.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Thanks for being here and testifying.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: You said that you were 15.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Well, that's very exciting that you spent the entire day.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: I saw that you've been waiting.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: I'm really grateful that you're engaging on the questions about AI.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Could you just share a little bit more about how you got into this work and what inspired you to put together the AI Treaty?

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: And is this something that you're also building out at school?

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Are you in high school?

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Do you go to school in the city?

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: And is this work that you're doing with your other peers?

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Could you speak into the mic and just share a little bit more?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Meredith
utterances.text: Sorry, you go.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Meredith
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: Yeah, I try to.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: I try to involve other members of my school in this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: What inspired me to work on this is I second what you said, that I could literally die if I don't work on this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: My life is in danger, so that's sort of my huge motivation for why I spend a lot of nights working on this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: I've also written a federal bill, a treaty on this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: I've written other things like, yeah, sure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: Like one thing New York can do on this matter that I've been working on is, like New York City specifically, could involve a bunch of students on this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: And New York could do a Manhattan project on AI safety to have students across New York work on AI safety's technical details to figure out how to make sure AI doesn't kill everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: That's what inspires me is that like this is a huge danger to everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: So this is incredibly important.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Could you share if at school there's any education on AI systems?

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: What's happening in your high school on the topic?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: At my school, one of my friends runs a club on AI covering these technical details.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: It's a huge topic for all the teachers at my school to talk about, oh, are these existential risks?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: One of the head people at my school is an expert in U.S.-China foreign policy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: The other day I was having...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: some discussion with someone who's more of a China hawk, one of my friends, on

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: the trade-off with safety versus race with China, which section six of my contract addresses with this really interesting algorithm.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: At the school level, what is happening is students are being involved and teachers are talking about it loosely, but there definitely could be like

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: across this different schools, we could have like a program where as an after school or as homework,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: we have students do projects on how do we make sure AI doesn't kill everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: Because we have like a million people in the public school system, about only 2,000 people are working on this problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: Even if only one in a thousand of the students take this seriously, that means a thousand new projects on this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: Which could be super valuable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: I also would encourage the city to do funding for AI safety work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: So far, globally, there's about only $2 billion in funding for this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: And the entire global economy is at stake, so it's worth investing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: A huge amount of money in this, maybe four, like four billion alone could triple it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: I'll also say that like the other ideas that I won't get to, I'll put on my website, aitreaty.base44.app today or tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: It'll be hopefully, and hopefully all of you guys send it to these AI companies with these very valuable messages of the contract, which could be the thing that solves the problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: You know, we keep talking about a deal, a treaty.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: This is that treaty.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: You know, I've spent a lot of time talking to experts about it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: If you have any...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: Problems with it, let me know and I'll fix them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: Jeez, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: Oh, and earlier, Julie Menon asked how we could balance safety with China.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: Section 6 of the contract addresses that really well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: I think the two...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: Did I cover everything?

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: I think you did.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Just leave your email address with us and your written testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
utterances.text: Yeah, this is my card.

chapters.summary: De La Rosa thanks the panel and encourages witnesses to stay in touch, noting future Council hearings will want youth voices. She begins calling a new set of names including James Hunter Horn, Martha Crane, and Rachel Levinson Waldman.
chapters.title: De La Rosa thanks youth panel and calls next witnesses

utterances.text: We have a few more folks to call, so we're going to thank this panel for coming in, and we're going to conclude, and we encourage you all to collect each other's contact information and follow the conversation offline as well.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: And we certainly love to stay in touch with some of you because...

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: There's going to be more hearings in the council that we'd love to hear the youth voice especially that's on this panel.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Okay, so I'm going to call a few more names, and if you're in the room, please come forward.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wes Friesen
