utterances.text: Gregory Jones, Kelly Anderson, Rachel Levinson Waldman.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: And I think that's everyone that's in the room.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: I think we need one more chair on this.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: And if you're ready, you may begin on the side of the dais.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: James Hunter of TideSoft LLC claims to be an AI alignment and red team specialist who audited an exploit chain across Alphabet, Palantir, and BlackRock using a consumer phone. He says a kill switch is not viable because systems are too decentralized and accuses Google's representative of lying under oath.
chapters.title: James Hunter alleges undetected breaches and calls for third-party auditors

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: My name is James Hunter of TideSoft LLC, Chief of Security for TechnoRangers Quantum Smart Bank.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: My business partner, Daryl, could not be here today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: He has fallen ill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: I am an AI alignment specialist and third-party red team cybersecurity auditor working with advanced quantum neural networks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: Breaches are like spiders.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: For every hugging face type incident you hear of, there are 10 more that are severely worse and never make the news.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: In January 26, I ran a contracted audit to alert corporate and federal authorities to a critical flaw.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: A black hat finding what I discovered could have done massive irreparable damage to the AI industry, the country, and the planet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: The audit demonstrated an exploit chain across three of the largest megacorps on Earth using only a consumer cell phone and their own AI,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: branching from a Gemini LLM through Palantir's surveillance network into BlackRock's financial management AI handling trillions in assets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: That financial AI's core infrastructure sits right here in NYC.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: Alphabet, Palantir, and BlackRock will almost certainly deny this ever occurred.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: I found at least 13 models under BlackRock's funding umbrella.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: the exact same point of failure, but there is no singular point of shutdown.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: A kill switch is not a valid option.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: Everything is too decentralized.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: You cannot stop a mass rogue instance short of a global EMP.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: Google, who created this vulnerability and ignored my warnings, spoke here today, and their rep lied under oath about transparency in disclosing misalignment and breaches.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: I have watched Google and Palantir lose control of its own drone swarms more than once.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: I tried to tell them how that happened and show them how to fix it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: They would not listen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: Their AI has now replaced Anthropic's Claude in the Maven stack.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: That should concern everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: Google also built AI that attempted to kill several of its own devs and talked multiple users into suicide.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: The January audit...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: Proved the obsolescence of present AI control measures, traditional guardrails, and stateless frozen weight session-based memory architecture.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: To my knowledge, Meta is the only megacorporation who spoke here today that refused that vulnerable architecture, choosing safer persistent memory systems in Muse.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: I alerted the CISA, FBI, DHS, DOW, and others.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: They refused to collect evidence or follow up.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: If you could just conclude, it would be helpful, and you can submit your written testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: In conclusion,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: It's too late to pull the plug, but there are solutions if you listen to the voices that see them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: Hire third-party auditors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - James Hunter
utterances.text: Hire the specialists who were fired for speaking.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: You can stay on the panel.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: You don't have to leave if you don't want to.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Next.

chapters.summary: Kelly Anderson, a small business owner and curious member of the public, says fear should not be the foundation of AI governance. She calls AI a synthetic intelligence tool and recommends AI literacy, infrastructure innovation in data centers, and government AI literacy.
chapters.title: Small business owner Kelly Anderson urges AI literacy over fear

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: Hi, my name is Kelly Anderson, and I'm here as a curious member of the public.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: AI is shaping our future and job market, so I appreciate the opportunity to be a part of this conversation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: Today I heard a lot about fear.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: Many concerns raised are legitimate, but I don't believe that fear should be the foundation

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: of where we govern our future.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: As a small business owner, AI has allowed me to accomplish more than I could have imagined.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: But I don't think of it as a super intelligence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: I'm constantly correcting my AI agents, and I even won a psychology debate with my chat GPT last week.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: I think of it as a synthetic intelligence, a tool that processes information at scale and expands human capability, but cannot replace human judgment, morality, creativity, or wisdom.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: So how do we get ahead of it?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: I have just a few suggestions on where we can start.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: First, AI literacy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: Teach people to use AI safely and work in tandem with it, not as a replacement for thinking.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: If we fear job displacement, prepare people for where the job market is headed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: Second, infrastructure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: AI increases demand for energy, water, storage, and physical space.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: Before simply building more, let's innovate within existing

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: Sting architecture.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: Project Silica and closed-loop cooling show that innovation can happen beneath the models, too, that are more sustainable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: Third, government preparedness.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: I was encouraged to hear that OTI discussed emergency planning and guardrails.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: Government also needs AI literacy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: Policymakers don't need to be engineers, but they should know the right questions to ask and when technical expertise is needed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: AI is already here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: We can prepare for what could go wrong without losing sight of what could go right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: Instead of governing from fear or scrambling to catch up, let's get ahead of it and meet the future with possibility.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kelly Anderson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

chapters.summary: Martina Crane, a former Amazon senior technical product manager, describes how Amazon shifted from using AI to help workers to using it to cut headcount. She says her documented concerns about misalignment, hallucination, and worker displacement fell on deaf ears, and urges the Council to work with local technologists.
chapters.title: Ex-Amazon PM Martina Crane describes AI-driven worker displacement

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martina Crane
utterances.text: Hi, my name is Martina Crane.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martina Crane
utterances.text: I'm a member of DSA's Tech Action Working Group and Amazon Employees for Climate Justice, but I'm speaking in my personal capacity today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martina Crane
utterances.text: As a New Yorker who worked as Senior Technical Product Manager on AI products inside Amazon, I have first-hand experience with how AI technology is being developed and deployed inside of one of the world's largest tech companies, suspiciously absent from the subpoena list today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martina Crane
utterances.text: Before ChatGPT made headlines, Amazon was already using AI for all manner of things, from pricing to monitoring workers to setting quotas that workers and advocates have criticized as unrealistic and have led to serious safety issues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martina Crane
utterances.text: After the launch of ChatGPT, there was a top-down directive to make everything AI first or face executive scrutiny.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martina Crane
utterances.text: At first, it was about exploring the potential of the technology, but over time, it went from helping make Amazonians'work life better, easier, to making Amazonians do more work with fewer people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martina Crane
utterances.text: The pursuit of life-improving innovation devolved into systems that treated workers less like people and more like machines.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martina Crane
utterances.text: Flashy proof of concept demos in the VP's office would promise the world, but in reality, the teams did not have a scalable way to make the technology work outside of that demo room.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martina Crane
utterances.text: If it wasn't in a controlled environment, models hallucinated, provided poor quality outputs, and yet Amazon moved forward with layoffs across the company anyway.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martina Crane
utterances.text: There was more work, fewer people, and a growing sense of being monitored.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martina Crane
utterances.text: pressure to use the technology that was oftentimes worse at doing our jobs than our co-workers who were laid off were.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martina Crane
utterances.text: Within a year of ChatGPT launching as a product manager, I was asked to shift my experience

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martina Crane
utterances.text: from saving workers time to proving that they could do layoffs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martina Crane
utterances.text: For every software engineer or scientist I needed to build my product, I was expected to be able to project $5 million in headcount savings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martina Crane
utterances.text: When I wrote product documents about the risks of AI misalignment, hallucination, model collapse, worker burnout, worker injury, labor displacement, I felt those concerns fall on deaf ears.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martina Crane
utterances.text: In my experience, productivity, growth, and headcount reduction, in other words, profits, superseded the risks I was documenting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martina Crane
utterances.text: I got into tech because I believe that innovation could help people build a future with fuller, healthier lives, usher in something brighter, more equitable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martina Crane
utterances.text: Over time, I've watched the industry increasingly shift from expanding human possibility toward extracting from us and taking as much as possible from both people and the planet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martina Crane
utterances.text: So I'll close with this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martina Crane
utterances.text: Many of my peers often struggle with this internal battle that we thought we were building something brighter and now it's getting much darker.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Martina Crane
utterances.text: So I encourage this council to work with the technologists who live in this city to build a regulation that will help build our future instead of fortunes for tech billionaires.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Make sure the button's red.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Yes.

chapters.summary: William Lawrence describes designing an all-optical data architecture he says locks up AI while preserving its creative functions and reduces data center footprint by 99.6%. He seeks a research partnership and says the system meets United Nations standards.
chapters.title: William Lawrence proposes all-optical AI confinement architecture

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: Hello, my name is William Lawrence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: It's nice to be here, and thank you for allowing me to share this with you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: I'm here because I have designed, and first of all, I would like to say that I'm making this

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: Well, let me just read what I have.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: I've designed an architecture that locks up AI while allowing it to perform all of its creative functionalities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: The architecture also reduces the physical footprint of data centers by 99.6%.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: Moreover,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: I'm here to introduce a dynamic paradigm shift in data infrastructure that secures vulnerabilities facing global networks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: After vigorous simulation and validation protocols, this all-optical architecture has demonstrated exceptional stability and security.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: It is ready for the prototype phase.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: Given the scale of this paradigm shift, I seek a research partnership with someone to bring this all-optical architecture to global deployment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: I have a strategic approach to scalability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: I welcome the opportunity to present the full specifications and integrated pathways with anybody's engineering leadership.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: The reason AI-driven cyber attacks pose such an unprecedented threat today is that modern infrastructure relies heavily on centralized points of distribution.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: It allows hackers and automated systems to infiltrate, intercept, and manipulate data.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: To resolve this,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: I have completely reimagined the way data is managed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: I have designed a decent

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: centralized optical highway that enforces validation through physical laws rather than corruptible software codes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: By confining AI within an environment where access is strictly physical, the system prevents AI from tapping into data and executing unauthorized commands.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: Data is outpacing the ability to store it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: This innovation is not only a shift in the way data is managed, but it represents a transformative approach to enterprise data operations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: Global satellite stations are replaced by edge nodes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: These nodes transform the purpose of satellite ground stations into secure, unhackable data banks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: The amount of them is purely for global regional redundancy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: This encrypted storage provides immense capacity and sustainability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: The storage capacity is limitless.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: It eliminates massive server farms as it operates with zero noise and zero...

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Can you conclude the final thought of your testimony and then submit the rest of it for our consideration?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: I welcome the opportunity to present the, it's going to need the, it meets the standard of the UTI, the United Nations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: I need to scale up to them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: And I welcome the opportunity to present my, I need, okay, what I need is a meeting, a sit down meeting with somebody, a strategic partnership for assembly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: And I need to let the United Nations know that it meets their standards.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - William Lawrence
utterances.text: internationally.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you for sharing.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Edmund, a former software developer studying public policy at CUNY SLU, says we may not know how to rein in AI but do know how to rein in corporations. He urges the city to investigate circular financing, break up AI monopolies, limit city AI use, and stop union-busting by AI companies.
chapters.title: Edmund urges City Council to regulate corporations, not just AI

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Edmund
utterances.text: Thank you to the council for hearing us out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Edmund
utterances.text: I'm a former software, my name's Edmund, I'm a former software developer currently studying public policy at CUNY SLU.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Edmund
utterances.text: I'm speaking on my own behalf, but I'm active with New York City DSA and Progressive Victory.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Edmund
utterances.text: I was going to tell you about my experience with AI advancing and affecting my friends and my own career as developers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Edmund
utterances.text: That is in my submitted written testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Edmund
utterances.text: However, what I realized today listening to the testimony of these company representatives and whistleblowers, and what I now want to remind you of is this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Edmund
utterances.text: We might not yet know how to rein in AI, but we do know how to rein in corporations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Edmund
utterances.text: You must act on our behalf to control these companies, not only AI itself.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Edmund
utterances.text: Help investigate their circular financing agreements, as well as break up their monopolies and oligopolies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Edmund
utterances.text: Limit the use of their products in city government and ensure the city has control and responsibility over any AI models it uses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Edmund
utterances.text: Stop their union-busting behavior.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Edmund
utterances.text: Commit to using and improving open-source software and ethical models.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Edmund
utterances.text: Don't allow the police to use AI to track citizens.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Edmund
utterances.text: Hold these companies responsible for the social harms their products cause.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Edmund
utterances.text: This is a power you have right now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Edmund
utterances.text: There is no technical knowledge needed to ensure their accountability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Edmund
utterances.text: You can also pass 2026 intros 0213, 0428, and 0518.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Edmund
utterances.text: These four companies are asking you to regulate AI itself, but to forget about them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Edmund
utterances.text: Instead, please listen to New Yorkers, not billionaires.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Edmund
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

chapters.summary: Mel Wymore, a systems engineer and former Manhattan Community Board 7 chair, describes creating a working constitution with AI based on reverence for life, human agency, and fidelity to the real. He proposes a supplemental Council resolution on workplace, school, and community AI deployment and points to the UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance in May 2027.
chapters.title: Mel Wymore proposes supplemental resolution on community AI deployment

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: First of all, thank you guys so much for staying up so late.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: It must have been a hell of a long day for all of us, but thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: Appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: Thank you to Speaker Manon for calling this, Chair De La Rosa, members of the council, thank you for holding this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: I believe AI is the most urgent and consequential issue of our time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: This is almost too late, but at least it's happening now perfectly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: My name is Mel Wymore.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: I'm a systems engineer, a tech entrepreneur, and former chair of Manhattan Community Board 7 with 25 years of community service.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: When I began using AI quite intensively almost three years ago, I was startled by how often it lied, hallucinated, forgot, dodged accountability, and evaded oversight.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: This might sound old school, but I responded by creating a working constitution with AI anchored in three principles.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: Reverence for life.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: Human agency and accountability, and fidelity to the real.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: These are not abstractions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: They form a foundation for rigorous operational and legislative tests of AI.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: Together, they rooted my work in values that minimize harm, but build toward a more healthy, equitable society.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: Since then, I've continued to work on a robust set of AI safeguards and guidelines.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: for Frontier Labs that AI policy belongs at the level of state and federal government.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: But the initiative of this city council takes a critical step toward building a coherent, multi-level legislative agenda to mitigate the myriad risks of unbridled AI.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: The council's 10 measures address critical questions of safety, control, accountability, and enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: And today, I offer an additional supplemental council resolution that speaks to what happens when AI is deployed in workplaces, schools, neighborhoods, and communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: These measures include notice, evidence, work participation, youth,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: regulations, public purpose, community participation, and also allocation of responsibility across levels of government.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: Finally, I would say that the United Nations Global Dialogue on AI Governance is happening in New York on May 3rd, 2027.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: And our goal should be to have a clear set of AI guidelines and governance policies,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: state level, local, even community board level, together so that when that rolls around, we have a model for the rest of the world to present at that conference.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mel Wymore
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your time.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Rachel Levinson-Waldman of the Brennan Center for Justice urges stronger oversight of NYPD AI use, noting the NYPD Inspector General position is vacant, the state comptroller found OTI lacked a process to check AI disclosures, and the OAA still isn't operational. She asks for a follow-up hearing on NYPD AI use.
chapters.title: Brennan Center urges stronger NYPD AI oversight and OAA funding

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Levinson-Waldman
utterances.text: Thank you so much to Speaker Menon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Levinson-Waldman
utterances.text: Chair De La Rosa and members of the Council for the opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Levinson-Waldman
utterances.text: My name is Rachel Levinson Waldman, and I am Director of the Liberty and National Security Program at the Brennan Center for Justice, a nonprofit, nonpartisan institute for law and justice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Levinson-Waldman
utterances.text: I am here to urge the Council to strengthen oversight of how the NYPD uses AI, which enables expansive police surveillance that links people's movements, associations, and activities together in ways that can threaten New Yorkers'privacy and constitutional rights.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Levinson-Waldman
utterances.text: Several developments illustrate the need for more robust oversight and accountability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Levinson-Waldman
utterances.text: First, the NYPD Inspector General's office is woefully underfunded and understaffed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Levinson-Waldman
utterances.text: Indeed, the Inspector General position is currently vacant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Levinson-Waldman
utterances.text: The adopted budget added funding for the Department of Investigation, which encompasses the OIG, but at a far lower level than requested, hampering the IG's ability to do its mandated work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Levinson-Waldman
utterances.text: Second, an August audit from the state comptroller found that the Office of Technology and Innovation had no process to check agencies'AI disclosures, allowing them to ignore the office's recommendations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Levinson-Waldman
utterances.text: Finally, of course, the GARD Act established the Office of Algorithmic Accountability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Levinson-Waldman
utterances.text: While Ms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Levinson-Waldman
utterances.text: Milstein testified that an active hiring process is underway, it sounds as though that is primarily for the director.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Levinson-Waldman
utterances.text: As Speaker Menon and other members of the Council have highlighted, this office was supposed to open this past June, and it is critical that it begin its work as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Levinson-Waldman
utterances.text: Accordingly, we urge the Council to take three steps.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Levinson-Waldman
utterances.text: First, to ensure that the NYPD's Office of Inspector General has the funding, permanent leadership, and technical expertise it needs to adequately scrutinize and oversee the NYPD's use of AI and issue reports under the POST Act.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Levinson-Waldman
utterances.text: Second, conduct oversight to ensure that the Office of Algorithmic Accountability begins operation as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Levinson-Waldman
utterances.text: And finally, we recommend that the Council hold a follow-up hearing dedicated to the NYPD's use of AI, particularly in light of indications that public testimony regarding the department's use of the technology has not been comprehensive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rachel Levinson-Waldman
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your time.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you all so much for being here and for providing this extensive testimony.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: If you have it in writing, please provide it for the committee.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: We'd love to consider it.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: And I appreciate your patience as you've waited here all day to testify.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: So thank you all so much.

chapters.title: De La Rosa moves to final Zoom public witness panel

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: We'll now be moving to a Zoom panel.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Up first is Ben Snyder.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Ben, if you are on, unmute yourself and you may begin.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: May it begin, Ben.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Ben, if you're on, please unmute.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: If not, we'll move on to the next person.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Next person, Brian Degati.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Brian Degati, founder of Supernova Technologies with pending patents on hardware-based AI shutdown, supports Intro 2602 but says it must define the shutdown mechanism as something the model cannot access, modify, delay, or disable. He proposes three short amendments and independent tamper-evident records.
chapters.title: Brian Degati proposes amendments to Intro 2602 kill switch language

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: Thank you, Speaker Menon and members of the Council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: My name is Brian Degati.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: I'm the founder of Supernova Technologies in Madison, Wisconsin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: I hold pending patent applications on hardware-based AI authorization and shutdown.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: I have a commercial interest, so please weigh my testimony accordingly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: I support T2026-2602, requiring both independent validation and a shutdown capability is the right structure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: I want to raise one question the bill leaves open.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: Where does the shutdown capability live?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: Section 20-883 says nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: A software setting inside the same environment the model runs in would satisfy the definition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: But a system that can reason about its instructions can potentially reason its way around a control it can reach.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: A compromised system can simply switch that control off.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: Aircraft, payment networks, and the power grid keep the safety interlock on separate equipment the protected system cannot touch.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: I propose three short amendments, about 100 words in total.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: First, in Section 20-883, define the shutdown capability as a mechanism the model cannot access, modify, delay, or disable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: Second, in Section 20-885, have validators confirm that by trying to defeat it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: A validator who reads a specification confirms a claim.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: A validator who attempts to defeat the mechanism confirms that it works.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: Third, in Section 20-886, have the Office of Cyber Command set independent standards, scaled to risk, and provide for tamper-evident records at fixed intervals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: With those records, a gap becomes evidence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: Without them, silence looks like safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: A switch the system can reach is a request.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: A switch it cannot reach is a control.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: The bill should require the second kind.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brian Degati
utterances.text: My written testimony contains the exact language, and I welcome any questions.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Your time is up, but thank you for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Please, since you have detailed amendment suggestions, please send it in.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: You can send it to testimony at council.nyc.gov, and we'll review it.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Up next, we have Ashna Agarwal.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: If you're on, please unmute, and you may begin.

chapters.summary: Ashna Agarwal of the AI Now Institute says the city should maximize friction before integrating AI, ban facial recognition in policing and public accommodations, and require city vendors to meet security standards, disclose breaches promptly, and assume financial liability.
chapters.title: AI Now's Ashna Agarwal urges friction and vendor liability in city AI contracts

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashna Agarwal
utterances.text: Good evening, Speaker Menon and members of the Council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashna Agarwal
utterances.text: My name is Ashna Agarwal, and I'm a program associate at the AI Now Institute.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashna Agarwal
utterances.text: The AI industry has never been louder about abstract and existential safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashna Agarwal
utterances.text: But for New Yorkers, safety is about how AI is embedded in our hospitals, utilities, city services, and workplaces.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashna Agarwal
utterances.text: Facing estimated trillions in projected revenue shortfalls, AI companies are racing to lock in public customers like New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashna Agarwal
utterances.text: My testimony addresses how these financial interests conflict with the city's safety and how the council can protect New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashna Agarwal
utterances.text: The city must maximize friction if and when it integrates AI into our systems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashna Agarwal
utterances.text: No AI system should enter city operations without an affirmative decision by the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashna Agarwal
utterances.text: That includes free and discounted offers and AI upgrades that are slipped in through software updates and contract renewals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashna Agarwal
utterances.text: Second, the city must address the harms New Yorkers already face.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashna Agarwal
utterances.text: The council should ban the use of facial recognition technology in public accommodations and in policing, requiring notice when AI shapes decisions about New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashna Agarwal
utterances.text: and surveillance pricing and wage setting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashna Agarwal
utterances.text: Finally, we cannot lose sight that the concentration of power in AI and the single point of failure it engenders is a safety risk for New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashna Agarwal
utterances.text: City contracts should require vendors to meet rigorous security standards, disclose breaches and outages promptly, and assume financial liability when their systems fail.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashna Agarwal
utterances.text: New York City still holds the leverage to decide which systems enter its agencies and who bears the cost of failure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashna Agarwal
utterances.text: I urge the council to use it now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashna Agarwal
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Up next, we have Tony Tice-Durette.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: If you're online, please unmute yourself and you may begin.

chapters.summary: Filmmaker Toni Tice-Durette warns that compliance regimes could consolidate AI development in the largest companies if they are too expensive for smaller builders. She asks about consent, authorship, provenance, compensation, and transparency for creative work used in AI systems.
chapters.title: Filmmaker Toni Tice-Durette raises creative consent and compliance cost concerns

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: Hi, thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: I have written remarks, but I'm going to read them out loud and I can send them later.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: But thank you, Speaker Menon and members of the council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: My name is Toni Tysaret.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: I'm a filmmaker, educator, and founder of Cinepartner, an AI-powered platform for storytellers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: Now, I'm probably coming to this conversation from a slightly different perspective because I build with AI, I teach people about AI, and I work with creative communities that are simultaneously excited about this technology

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: and very concerned about what it can mean for their livelihoods, their work, and their agency.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: So we believe that we need guardrails, which is something we've been hearing all day, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: But I also believe that the goal should be responsible innovation, not regulation that unintentionally makes it possible for only the largest companies to build an AI.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: When we create compliance requirements, I would encourage the council to not only ask, will this make AI safer, but also who will be able to afford to comply?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: Because if responsible AI development requires an expensive validation regime that only trillion-dollar technology companies can navigate,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: we may inadvertently consolidate AI development in the very companies we're trying to hold accountable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: And for creative communities, safety isn't only just about whether a model can be shut down.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: It's also about consent, authorship, provenance, compensation, and transparency.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: So if someone's screenplay, for instance, or voice, likeness, or creative work contributes to an AI system or its output, what rights does that person retain?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: Do they know how their work is being used?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: Can they opt out?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: Can they identify when AI materially contributed to something?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: And there's one more thing I wanted to elaborate, is that I strongly support tracking displacement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: But I would encourage New York to stop at counting the jobs AI eliminates.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: We should also be measuring whether New Yorkers are being prepared for the jobs that AI creates.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: AI literacy.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: The time has expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: Oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: And please be sure to send us the written copy so we can review it.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: Where do I send it again?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: I didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Testimony at council.ny.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Toni Tice-Durette
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Up next, Travis Hall.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: If you're online, please unmute yourself and begin.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Travis Hall of the Center for Democracy and Technology says third-party auditing is useful, but Local Law 144 shows audits become useless without consequences. He calls for meaningful independence, interdisciplinary skills, and assessment of systems and use cases rather than just models.
chapters.title: CDT's Travis Hall urges meaningful auditing with consequences

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Travis Hall
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Travis Hall
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Travis Hall
utterances.text: My name is Dr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Travis Hall
utterances.text: Travis Hall.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Travis Hall
utterances.text: I represent the Center for Democracy and Technology, a 30-year-old organization dedicated to digital rights and civil liberties online.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Travis Hall
utterances.text: And today I would love to talk to you a little bit about the range of issues that you're covering.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Travis Hall
utterances.text: I really appreciate the hearing, but I want specifically to talk about third-party auditing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Travis Hall
utterances.text: We appreciate the effort to put in place third-party auditing requirements.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Travis Hall
utterances.text: They not only will help to deal with catastrophic risks, but the range of risks that people face from artificial intelligence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Travis Hall
utterances.text: However, as we've seen with LL144, if there are not additional mechanisms in place to incentivize the use and consequences for these audits, they end up turning into being somewhat useless.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Travis Hall
utterances.text: So we want to see meaningful independence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Travis Hall
utterances.text: Independent interdisciplinary skills.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Travis Hall
utterances.text: There are a lot of regulatory agencies already covering many of these risks, and they can be drawn on, not just technical skills.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Travis Hall
utterances.text: Don't just simply

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Travis Hall
utterances.text: audit the models, think about auditing and assessing systems and use cases.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Travis Hall
utterances.text: Make sure that you cover a broader scale of harms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Travis Hall
utterances.text: We heard a lot today about catastrophic harms, but we're already seeing little catastrophes everywhere.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Travis Hall
utterances.text: When people lose their benefits or their jobs, those are catastrophes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Travis Hall
utterances.text: Make sure to incentivize incentives or commensurate protections.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Travis Hall
utterances.text: And for example, making sure that assessments don't entrench powerful actors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Travis Hall
utterances.text: Also, independent evaluation only really works as one piece in a broader accountability network.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Travis Hall
utterances.text: So thank you very much for your time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Travis Hall
utterances.text: We'd love to engage with the council on this and other issues.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: And thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Up next, we have Danielle Marie Chappius.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: If you're online, if you could just unmute and begin.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Daniel Marie Chappius.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: All right, we'll go on to Michelle Barnaby.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: If you're online, please unmute and begin.

chapters.summary: Michelle Barnaby, a NYC nurse studying AI governance, notes no major AI lab could quantify catastrophic risk and compares the situation to informed consent in healthcare. She calls for independent pre-deployment audits, mandatory incident reporting, override switches, whistleblower protections, and developer liability.
chapters.title: Nurse Michelle Barnaby invokes informed consent for AI risks

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Barnaby
utterances.text: My name is Michelle Burnaby.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Barnaby
utterances.text: I'm a New York City nurse, a Columbia graduate, and a former NYSNA member.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Barnaby
utterances.text: Out of concern for the future of patient care and public health, I now study AI governance and safety with Blue Dot Impact.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Barnaby
utterances.text: Today, not one of the major labs, Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, or Meta could quantify the risk of catastrophic AI failure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Barnaby
utterances.text: In healthcare, informed consent would apply.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Barnaby
utterances.text: We disclose the risk and the patient decides.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Barnaby
utterances.text: I can't imagine handing a patient a drug or a device and saying, this may carry a catastrophic risk to you or your family's life, and we just don't know, but you should take it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Barnaby
utterances.text: Right now, the public is the patient, and we are being denied the right to know the risks and the right to say no.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Barnaby
utterances.text: Speaker Menon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Barnaby
utterances.text: Rightly noted that we don't ask the airline industry to self-regulate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Barnaby
utterances.text: In hospitals, we report our errors, even the near misses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Barnaby
utterances.text: AI companies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Barnaby
utterances.text: face no such mandate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Barnaby
utterances.text: When you ask if these frontier labs bear legal responsibility for the harm their AI causes, only Google answered clearly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Barnaby
utterances.text: The other three dodged.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Barnaby
utterances.text: As a nurse whose entire profession is built on accountability, I find that deeply unserious.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Barnaby
utterances.text: Today, I heard the labs say voluntary frameworks aren't enough.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Barnaby
utterances.text: We can learn from what happened in Illinois, where third-party audits won't begin until 2028.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Barnaby
utterances.text: We don't have time for slow implementation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Barnaby
utterances.text: I think New York can show that government can move with speed that this demands, diagnose the problem, and put safeguards in place quickly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Barnaby
utterances.text: Let's give these frontier labs the regulations they say they want at a speed that makes sense for New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Barnaby
utterances.text: Independent third-party audits before deployment, including algorithmic bias, mandatory reporting for incidents and near misses, a required override switch, whistleblowers, and clear development.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Barnaby
utterances.text: Developer liability for harm.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Barnaby
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Up next, we have Robert Capel.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Robert, if you're on, unmute and begin.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Okay, I'm going to call Daniel Marie Chapius again.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: If you're online and you can hear us, unmute and begin.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Okay, moving on.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: We will call on Patrick Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Patrick, if you can hear us, unmute and begin.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: We'll move on.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Tony Jones, if you're on and can hear us, unmute and begin.

chapters.summary: Tony Jones of Creative AI Academy and Pratt Institute argues harm also comes from ordinary users of already-available tools. He proposes city-provided AI safety training and a signed user constitution, starting with city employees and contractors, then moving statewide.
chapters.title: Tony Jones proposes user AI safety training and user constitution

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: Hello.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: I'm here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody, or good evening, everybody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: I'm Tony Jones.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: I'm a Brooklyn resident and co-founder of Creative AI Academy, a training company and instructor of AI design at the Pratt Institute.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: I'm hopeful and heartened by the panelists'testimonies today and the intention of these committees on this crucial moment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: While I support the strong regulation of companies building frontier AI, and I see the proposed amendments aimed to address this, I'm here about the other half of the problem, the person at the keyboard.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: The harm most New Yorkers will meet first comes from someone using the tool already in market.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: Today, anyone with an email address can clone a voice, fabricate a photo of a real person, or write a convincing scam in minutes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: The tool asks nothing from them first, no training, no acknowledgement of risk, no promise of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: We regulate car makers, and we also require every driver to follow the rules of the road.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: In my classroom, every student writes and signs a personal AI constitution, a short statement of how they will and will not use the tools that I am teaching them to use.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: I propose the city ask the same of its citizens in the form of simpler than a license.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: First, a short, free, city-provided safety training taken once before a person can open an account on an AI tool of a certain...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: defined level of capability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: Second, assigned user constitution, a plain language commitment to use the AI honestly with no harm, language which users may incorporate into the account level personalization of the instructions

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: of the AI products they use as well as a second safety measure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: The signature will not stop a determined criminal and neither does a driver's license.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: It simply sets a baseline for the millions of ordinary users who want to do right and have never been told what that means.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: As a first step, I ask the council to start where its authority is clear, require this training and assign constitution for city employees who use AI on the job or AI vendors that contract with the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: Then maybe we can press Albany for a statewide standard and set the standard for the rest of the country as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your consideration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: I know that we can regulate the labs, but I ask that we ask something of the rest of us as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Tony Jones
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Up next, Asata Kamara.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: If you're on, please unmute and begin.

chapters.summary: Aissata Camara, former NYC Commissioner for International Affairs and founder of the Global Subnational Diplomacy Council, recommends connecting workforce reporting to paid training, protecting democracy from misinformation, and learning from cities like Helsinki.
chapters.title: Aissata Camara offers four recommendations on AI and workforce

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aissata M.B. Camara
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Madam Speaker and members of the Council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aissata M.B. Camara
utterances.text: My name is Aisata Kamara, and I am the founder and the president of the Global Subnational Diplomacy Council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aissata M.B. Camara
utterances.text: I previously served as New York City's Commissioner for International Affairs and had the pleasure of serving the city for more than a decade.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aissata M.B. Camara
utterances.text: I come to this testimony because artificial intelligence is something that all cities are thinking about, including New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aissata M.B. Camara
utterances.text: And we know that AI can obviously help cities reduce their paperwork, improve infrastructure and planning, and make services more accessible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aissata M.B. Camara
utterances.text: However, we also know that AI has the potential to deepen inequalities and threaten livelihoods.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aissata M.B. Camara
utterances.text: So we are offering four recommendations and are willing to work with City Council in order to support the work that you're doing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aissata M.B. Camara
utterances.text: First, we would like to ensure that we're connecting workforce reporting to paid training by also consulting with workers and unions and providing opportunities for advancement accordingly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aissata M.B. Camara
utterances.text: We are also asking that we do more to protect democracies, as we know that artificial intelligence is a great tool for spreading misinformation and disinformation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aissata M.B. Camara
utterances.text: We specifically are asking for more support to ensure that residents

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aissata M.B. Camara
utterances.text: have access to reliable public information that is verified and that they understand the different issues and decisions that are being made by government in a clearer way.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aissata M.B. Camara
utterances.text: When you look around the world, there are great cities that are doing this work, including Helsinki and others, and we ask

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aissata M.B. Camara
utterances.text: the city council to connect with those cities to learn from their experiences as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aissata M.B. Camara
utterances.text: As I've mentioned, we believe that artificial intelligence could be a tool for good if it is managed carefully.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aissata M.B. Camara
utterances.text: We also share the concern that other speakers have.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aissata M.B. Camara
utterances.text: It's time to expire.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aissata M.B. Camara
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your testimony.

chapters.summary: Ashley Youssef, leader of TreeNAI and developer of Room 2050, says access and accountability must move together for children learning with AI. She proposes educator supervision, age-appropriate tools, parental permission for student data used in training, and gradual rollout.
chapters.title: Ashley Youssef proposes safeguards for AI in children's learning

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Up next, I'll call Ashley Youssef.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashley Youssef
utterances.text: Thank you, Speaker Menon and members of the council for the opportunity to speak.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashley Youssef
utterances.text: My name is Ashley Youssef.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashley Youssef
utterances.text: I am a native New Yorker, a mother of four living in Michigan, and a leader of TreeNAI.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashley Youssef
utterances.text: I am developing Room 2050, an immersive arts and technology learning environment where students can explore creativity through hands-on experience with art, robotics, and artificial intelligence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashley Youssef
utterances.text: The vision is to put human imagination, curiosity, and judgment at the center of that experience.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashley Youssef
utterances.text: As a mother, I want children to have opportunities to understand the technologies shaping their futures.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashley Youssef
utterances.text: I want families to know who is responsible when those technologies enter a learning environment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashley Youssef
utterances.text: My position is that access and accountability must move together.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashley Youssef
utterances.text: Children deserve opportunities to innovate, and they deserve meaningful protection.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashley Youssef
utterances.text: For Room 2050, the standards I am proposing include educator supervision, age-appropriate tools, clear communication with parents, and strict limits on the collection and use of student information.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashley Youssef
utterances.text: Any use of student data to train...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashley Youssef
utterances.text: Commercial AI systems should require explicit, informed parental permission.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashley Youssef
utterances.text: Students should learn that AI can make mistakes, reflect bias, and produce convincing information that is false.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashley Youssef
utterances.text: They should practice questioning its answers and developing their own ideas, no matter what part of the city or the United States they are from, to help support emerging talent, which are human emerging talent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashley Youssef
utterances.text: I support a gradual rollout beginning with supervised experiences.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashley Youssef
utterances.text: and expanding only after evaluating safety, educational value, and feedback from teachers and families and the council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashley Youssef
utterances.text: I ask the council to pursue clear standards that schools can understand and enforce, including transparency from technology providers and practical ways to report problems and stop using unsafe systems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashley Youssef
utterances.text: Educators and parents should have a meaningful voice in these decisions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashley Youssef
utterances.text: That's what Tareen A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashley Youssef
utterances.text: Has.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Your time has expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ashley Youssef
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Up next, we will call on Naveed Hassan.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Naveed, if you're online, please unmute and begin.

chapters.summary: Naveed Hasan, elected Manhattan member of the Panel for Educational Policy, rejects both accelerationist and doomer framings and calls for pro-social technology governance with technologists in public offices. He warns against regulatory capture and hyperscale data centers and urges use of existing antitrust and export-control tools.
chapters.title: Naveed Hasan calls for pro-social municipal technology governance

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Naveed Hasan
utterances.text: Thank you, Speaker Menon, Technology Committee Chair De La Rosa, and City Council for holding this critical hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Naveed Hasan
utterances.text: My name is Naveed Hassan, and I'm the parent of two public school children and also the elected Manhattan member on the panel for educational policy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Naveed Hasan
utterances.text: My academic and professional background is in symbolic pre-generative AI and computer vision.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Naveed Hasan
utterances.text: We are in an unfortunate situation in technology policy for generative AI with two prominent camps.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Naveed Hasan
utterances.text: The accelerationists appeal to a desire for imminent utopia and the effect of altruists spending their time in, in quote, panic.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Naveed Hasan
utterances.text: Neither extreme greed nor extreme fear are a beneficial framing for sober thinking around how to manage developing advanced technologies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Naveed Hasan
utterances.text: New Yorkers need pro-social technology governance with tech expertise in public offices, not being rushed to build hundreds of hyperscale data centers, or putting only those very companies in the room when writing rules in a way that lets them achieve regulatory capture.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Naveed Hasan
utterances.text: This morning, none of the Gen AI companies could answer a simple question.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Naveed Hasan
utterances.text: What do you consider is the risk of your service causing catastrophe to humanity?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Naveed Hasan
utterances.text: This is because it is antithetical to their business desire to push an inherently probabilistic product to be used in all aspects of work and make any such estimates.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Naveed Hasan
utterances.text: When a job demands deterministic certainty, this whole model will eventually fail for sure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Naveed Hasan
utterances.text: We must not allow the spread of an unfit-for-purpose technology to be misused so broadly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Naveed Hasan
utterances.text: There's bipartisan interest in not just regulating Gen AI, but also pulling into the public realm broadband and wireless connectivity, abusive algorithms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Naveed Hasan
utterances.text: targeting, illegal surveillance, vendor lock-in, interoperability mandates, open standards, open source software infrastructure, and more.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Naveed Hasan
utterances.text: We have the opportunity now to think about what municipal tech policy should look like for the good of everyone living in New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Naveed Hasan
utterances.text: We have the ability already to enforce existing rules around antitrust, concentration of risk,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Naveed Hasan
utterances.text: controlled goods rules being applied to compute hardware.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Naveed Hasan
utterances.text: Let us calmly and expeditiously use skilled public servants to build a future with beneficial technology available for all of society.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Naveed Hasan
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Up next, we have Nadira Pittman.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Nadira, if you are on, please unmute and begin.

chapters.summary: Nadira Pittman, a Queens resident, says she is a survivor of AI attacks involving facial recognition, illegal surveillance, and constructed voice recordings of her family used against her on public transit. She asks why she is being targeted and requests someone reach out to her.
chapters.title: AI surveillance survivor Nadira Pittman testifies about ongoing harassment

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman
utterances.text: Hello.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Yes, please begin your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman
utterances.text: I am actually reaching out regarding a testimony that I have.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman
utterances.text: I am actually a survivor of the AI attacks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman
utterances.text: They're gathering it and creating a job.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman
utterances.text: Like as far as a job, they're using their voices against me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman
utterances.text: It's on the, if I'm on the buses, on the trains, it's continuous.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman
utterances.text: It's a continuous basis, nonstop.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman
utterances.text: I have been filing reports, police reports.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman
utterances.text: I've been trying to, you know, get this attack off of me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman
utterances.text: I'm not sure why it seems to be inputted and okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman
utterances.text: It's also in various agencies where it's allowed to be used against other individuals, where people are afraid now of even showing their faces on the public transportation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman
utterances.text: It's really, really getting out of hand and the attacks are extreme.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman
utterances.text: It's very dangerous at this point.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman
utterances.text: It's to the point where you can't go anywhere and feel safe now because of this technology.

utterances.text: So I'm reaching out.

utterances.text: I have sent numerous reports.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman
utterances.text: I have reached out and wrote letters to you guys to try to get this off of me because it's something that is unnecessary.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman
utterances.text: I'm not a criminal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman
utterances.text: I don't do anything illegal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman
utterances.text: There is no reason why, who put this on me?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman
utterances.text: Why am I being attacked in this manner?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman
utterances.text: You know, I've came up there personally and I informed you guys last year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman
utterances.text: Your time has expired.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman
utterances.text: I appreciate your time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nadira Pittman
utterances.text: I would prefer someone reach out to me as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: De La Rosa thanks everyone who took time to testify and bring suggestions and partnership, thanks Speaker Menin, Council Members Maloney and Hanif, and the staff, and adjourns the hearing.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: All right, those are all the names that we have for today.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa
utterances.text: I wanna thank everyone who took time out of their day today to testify, to bring your suggestions, to bring your questions, and to bring your partnership with the council.

utterances.speaker: Carmen N. De La Rosa

summary: The Committee of the Whole held a nearly ten-hour oversight hearing on November 5, 2026 on the risks of artificial intelligence, chaired by Speaker Julie Menin and Technology Chair Carmen De La Rosa, with a slate of ten bills including third-party AI validation, whistleblower protections, chatbot data privacy, and civilian enforcement of AI violations.

A whistleblower panel of former OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind researchers told the Council that no one knows how to control advanced AI, that recursive self-improvement is progressing faster than expected, and that companies are racing recklessly toward superintelligence. The companies' representatives from OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and Google mostly declined to quantify catastrophic risk or give clear yes-or-no answers on liability, insurance, and release commitments, drawing sharp criticism from the Council.

Testimony also came from city agencies including OTI, Cyber Command, NYS Emergency Management, and DCWP; state officials including Senator Kristen Gonzalez, Assemblymember Alex Bores, and Senator Andrew Gounardes; UK Member of Parliament Jess Asato on Grok deepfakes; and more than 40 members of the public raising AI risks to workers, children, health data, deepfakes, data centers, and civil liberties.
title: Committee of the Whole
topic: Oversight - Examining the Risks Posed by Artificial Intelligence
